items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: He said, “Well I’ll tell you what,” he said, “do you know Prez?” I said, “No.”

ctx.x: But I knew that I did, you know, but I had low self esteem so that really lifted my self esteem up a couple of notches. He said, “Well I’ll tell you what,” he said, “do you know Prez?” I said, “No.” He said, “All right, so then why don’t you learn a Prez solo?” And so he gave me “Tickle Toe.”
That’s usually the way instructors do too. Instead of — he went backwards on you, right?

items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said, 'What about Lester Young? What about Prez?' I said, 'Oh, Prez. Oh no, I don‟t know Prez.'

ctx.x: Can you talk a little bit about Lennie as a person? How was he? He seemed to be…

Oh… Oh, Lennie was, was lovely. He was a wonderful man. He was… I loved him most of all because he was a Bird freak. He loved Charlie Parker. My very first lesson was… I went in there and he said, “Okay. This is what I want you to do.” I said, “Yes, Lennie.” He said, uh, “I want you to learn this Charlie Parker tune and the solo.” And I said, “Oh, I know it „cause of Detroit.” So he said, uh, “Well, let‟s hear you sing it.” I think it was Now Is The Time. I believe it was. And so, uh… I mean, I didn‟t do a great…
He sounds, he sounds quite versatile because he‟s known as such an arch theorist.
